sections.h2: Where do you file a deed for an Orange County house?
sections.html:
Go to Suite 300 of the Gateway Center, 228 S Churton Street, Hillsborough, NC 27278. Weekday hours run from 8 in the morning to 5 in the afternoon.

A seller in Chapel Hill, Carrboro or Efland files at the same Hillsborough counter as everyone else in the county. The county tells visitors to park in the deck directly behind the Gateway Center. Its recording page also lists an e-recording option, which lets a title office send documents without a drive across town.

  • Place: Gateway Center, Suite 300, on S Churton Street
  • Open: Monday to Friday until 5 p.m., closed on holidays
  • Parking: the deck behind the building
  • Records search: the county's document inquiry website

sections.h2: What extras does the Orange County fee schedule list?
sections.html:
The schedule dated October 1, 2026 starts with the familiar statewide amounts, then adds a long list of smaller charges. The ones below are most likely to turn up in a home sale or an estate.

Selected Orange County Register of Deeds charges, October 1, 2026 schedule
ServiceCharge as printed
Non-standard document$25 per document
Each party name past the twentieth$2
Certified plat copy$5 per page
Uncertified plat copy$3 per page
Right of way plans or highway maps$21 first page, $5 each added page
Notary public oath of office$10
Notice of satisfactionNo charge

Deeds themselves are $26 for 15 pages and mortgages $64 for 35 pages. Recording payments can be made by cash, certified check, money order, personal or business check or card, with American Express and Apple Pay excluded.

sections.h2: What stamp tax applies to an Orange County deed?
sections.html:
The FAQ on the county site says the stamp is $1 for each $500, or fractional part of $500, of value conveyed. The fee table prints the same idea as $2 per thousand for deeds from August 1, 1991 on.

Older rates appear only for reading history: $1 per thousand from January 1, 1968 through July 31, 1991, and $1.10 per thousand earlier. The seller owes the tax at the counter before filing. For the exact stamp amount on your price, ask your closing attorney rather than guessing.

sections.h2: What will Orange County staff do, and what will they send you elsewhere for?
sections.html:
They issue certified copies of deeds recorded in the county and help owners find a plat by book and page. They send title searches to attorneys.

The county FAQ says a title search must come from an attorney, or a paralegal under an attorney's supervision. It adds that changing a name on a recorded deed takes a new deed, and it suggests legal counsel for anyone not used to drafting one. That advice fits an inherited house or a divorce, where a closing attorney can draft the right instrument ahead of a sale.

  • Certified copies of recorded deeds: yes, at the scheduled fee
  • Plat copies: certified $5 a page, uncertified $3 a page
  • Title search: attorney or supervised paralegal
  • Changing names on a deed: a new deed is needed

sections.h2: Which county gets the deed when a house sits near a county line?
sections.html:
The county where the land lies. Registration there fixes the deed's rank against rival claims, whatever city the buyer or lender calls home.

Orange County's rate codes include city entries for Durham and Mebane, a reminder that those towns reach into the county. If part of a parcel is in another county, ask the closing attorney which office takes the deed and the excise tax. A deed is not safe against later claims until the register of deeds has stamped it.

sections.h2: What else does the Orange County office file?
sections.html:
Besides deeds, it takes plats, notices of satisfaction, assumed business names and Uniform Commercial Code filings. The county's recording page links to document standards, an inquiry tool for submitting and searching document questions, and a guide to registering an assumed name.

UCC filings fall under Chapter 25, Article 9 of the General Statutes. The fee page prints $38 for an initial filing, correction, amendment or termination of up to two pages, $45 for three to ten pages and $2 for each page beyond ten. An owner who financed fixtures or equipment tied to a property should ask the office whether a filing exists before listing. Marriage licenses cost $60 and are valid at once for sixty days.

sections.h2: What should an Orange County seller settle before the deed is filed?
sections.html:
Settle the mortgage payoff, the tax bill and the stamp tax. Each one changes what the closing attorney sends to Hillsborough.

  • A lender's satisfaction of a deed of trust is recorded free, so ask the lender how long it takes to send one.
  • The yearly property tax is a lien from its listing date and the bill is due September 1. Ask Orange County Tax Administration for the balance.
  • The stamp tax comes out of the seller's proceeds at closing.

Sellers who want to skip repairs and showings sometimes pick a cash buyer. The filing steps look the same either way.

sections.h2: What other counter services share the Orange County office?
sections.html:
The same Gateway Center office issues marriage licenses, certified vital records and notary oaths, and it runs a passport service. Those lines can mean a wait on a busy day, so schedule a deed filing for a time when you can wait.

A marriage license costs $60 per license. Applications are taken daily from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. except on holidays, and card payments carry a 2.5% convenience fee with a $2 minimum. A passport execution fee is $35 and a passport photo is $17. Certified copies of births, deaths and marriages are $10 each. Military discharge copies carry no charge. Some of these services take only certain forms of payment, so read the payment list on the fee page before you go.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about housing in Orange County?
sections.html:
Survey data from 2020 to 2024 gives Orange County a middle owner-occupied home value of $459,500, and owners occupy 63.8% of homes.

Median gross rent is $1,496 and typical monthly owner costs with a mortgage are $2,221. There are 57,342 households and 64,913 housing units. Nearly 62% of adults over 25 hold a bachelor's degree or better, and 12.9% of residents were born abroad. Builders took out 666 permits in 2025. A seller pricing a house here should lean on recent nearby sales rather than a county-wide median.

sections.h2: What should you bring to the Orange County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Bring the signed, notarized original deed and payment for the recording fee and the stamp tax. A photo ID matters for vital records: the county accepts a driver license with photograph, a state identification card or a passport.

Someone collecting a certificate for another person, such as an agent or attorney, must show papers proving authority. For deeds that run long, list many parties or use an odd page size, phone the office first. Added-page, non-standard document and extra-name charges can apply to those.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Orange County NC Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: 228 S Churton Street, Suite 300, in the Gateway Center, Hillsborough, NC 27278. The county lists weekday hours of 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost in Orange County?
faqs.a: Its fee page shows $26 for the first 15 pages and $4 for every page after that. Add $25 if the document is non-standard, and $2 for each party name past 20.

faqs.q: How much is the deed stamp tax in Orange County?
faqs.a: The county prints $1 for each $500 of value, or part of $500, and shows $2 per thousand in its table. The seller pays it at the counter before filing.

faqs.q: Does the Orange County office run title searches?
faqs.a: No. The county says an attorney, or a paralegal working under one, must do a title search. Staff can point you to the recorded documents.
Yes. Its Recording and Real Estate page lists E-Recording. Call the Hillsborough office to confirm how to set it up before you plan around it.
